offer.problem: Useful lessons are scattered across unfinished notes.
offer.promise: Turn one owned source into a reviewable lesson outline.

source.text: Start with a question your readers ask. Select one passage from your own notes. Write a worked example, explain its limits, and invite the reader to try it.

drafts.pageHeadline: Give your scattered teaching notes a first lesson.
drafts.pageBody: This example workbook helps you choose one learner question, find a useful passage in your own notes, and turn it into a worked example. Join the waitlist to help shape the first edition.
drafts.welcomeSubject: What have you been meaning to teach?
drafts.welcomeBody:
Thanks for joining the example workbook waitlist.

Start with one question your learners keep asking. You do not need a complete course to answer it well.

Reply with that question and the kind of notes you already have. Your answer will help shape the workbook.

Example lesson workbook
drafts.lessonSubject: Try this with one passage from your notes
drafts.lessonBody:
Pick one passage from notes you own.

Write a short example that shows the idea at work. Then add one sentence explaining where the example stops being useful.

That gives your learner both a starting point and a boundary. What question would you add to help them try it?

Example lesson workbook
drafts.invitationBody:
If you have useful teaching notes but no clear first lesson, that is the problem this workbook is designed to address.

Tell us what you teach and what you want a learner to be able to try.

Join the workbook waitlist: https://example.com/waitlist

Example lesson workbook
drafts.linkedin:
A useful first lesson can begin with one learner question and one passage from your own notes.

Write an example. Explain its limits. Invite the reader to try it.

I am developing a workbook around that sequence. If your teaching ideas are scattered across unfinished notes, what would help you choose the first one?

Join the workbook waitlist: https://example.com/waitlist
drafts.searchAnswer: To turn teaching notes into a first lesson, choose one question your learners ask. Find a passage in your own notes that addresses it. Write an example, explain the example's limits, and ask the learner to try the method. This is a starting structure, not evidence that every topic can be taught in one short lesson.
